messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [Redacted]
Sex: Female
Age: 29 Years
Hospital: Orašje County Hospital (Bosnia and Herzegovina)
Admission Date: [Redacted]
Discharge Date: [Redacted]
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
A 29-year-old female was admitted to the Department of Surgery with a history of recurrent colicky right upper quadrant abdominal pain. The patient was diagnosed as having multiple gallstones within the gallbladder on abdominal ultrasonography. Routine hematological and biochemical test results were normal. The patient underwent elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy, and there were no complications during the procedure, or postoperatively. The patient was discharged on the third postoperative day. 

Pathology Report:
Histologically, microscopic slides from the gallbladder body showed that almost the entire cylindrical epithelium of the mucosa was missing. There was a moderate mixed inflammatory cell infiltrate in the submucosa, and the muscular layer was slightly hypertrophic, which is consistent with chronic cholecystitis. The most unusual feature of the slide from the body of the gallbladder was the presence of large dilated vessels within the muscular layer extending into the submucosa and mucosa. The appearance of angiodysplasia of the gallbladder and its endothelial lining was confirmed immunohistochemically using CD34, CD31, and podoplanin (D2-40) monoclonal antibodies. 

Follow-up:
The patient remained healthy at 6-year follow-up. 

Summary:
The patient, a 29-year-old woman, underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy for multiple gallstones within the gallbladder. The histopathological findings revealed chronic cholecystitis with the unusual feature of angiodysplasia of the gallbladder. There were no complications during the procedure, and the patient was discharged on the third postoperative day. The patient remained healthy at the 6-year follow-up.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
Admission was for elective cholecystectomy for symptomatic multiple gallstones; histology showed chronic cholecystitis, and angiodysplasia was an incidental finding. Gallstones with chronic cholecystitis fall under cholelithiasis in chapter K (digestive system). The category is K80.

CODE: K80
